title: Logging and Application State
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of logging and application state in a FastAPI application.
Apply or interpret one example related to python logging.
Identify one limitation or failure case and describe how to verify it.

content.intro: This lesson covers logging and application state within structuring and configuring applications. Use the supplied syllabus topics as the coverage checklist, then connect them to the worked example and the verification task.
content.why_it_matters: You will use logging and application state to build APIs whose contracts and behavior are understandable to both clients and maintainers. The practical aim is operational evidence, configuration discipline, failure detection and safe recovery.

content_blocks.title: Core idea
content_blocks.text: Logging and Application State matters because it is part of structuring and configuring applications. In practice, focus on operational evidence, configuration discipline, failure detection and safe recovery. A framework feature only helps when its assumptions match the application; keep input validation, business policy and side effects distinguishable.

items.title: Python logging
items.text: For python logging, collect measurable evidence from a local or staging environment. Keep configuration environment-specific, avoid logging secrets, establish a rollback path, and do not claim performance or availability without measurements.

items.text: Use request-specific state as a design decision rather than a keyword to memorize. State the input and expected result, identify the boundary conditions, and connect the concept to the surrounding FastAPI request lifecycle.

items.title: Avoiding secrets in logs
items.text: Treat avoiding secrets in logs as a trust-boundary concern. Verify identity and permissions on the server, use least privilege, keep secrets outside source control, and write negative tests for unauthorized access.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Logging and Application State
content_blocks.code:
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    app.state.ready = True
    yield
    app.state.ready = False

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
content_blocks.expected_output: The lifespan setup runs before requests are served and cleanup runs at shutdown.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Run locally and watch startup/shutdown logs; do not use this example to store secrets in code.
content_blocks.reset_steps: For read-only examples, no reset is needed. For any example that writes state, use a disposable local database/test fixture; record the starting state and clean up only lab data. Never use production credentials or real personal data.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a code fragment without checking its assumptions.
common_mistakes.why: Installed versions, imported types, application structure and external services affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: State assumptions; check the versioned official docs; run a minimal local test and add one failure case.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating one happy-path response as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Invalid input, permissions, concurrency, timeouts and cleanup are not exercised by a single request.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused normal and negative tests and record exact expected status/body.

common_mistakes.why: Even short examples may mutate records, reveal data or affect availability.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic inputs and a disposable environment; review security, cleanup and rollback before promotion.
